title: Mixed Precision Training
before: Training ran in 32-bit floating point throughout.
problem: Memory and bandwidth, not arithmetic, were the binding constraints on model size.
breakthrough: Keep weights in 16-bit for the forward and backward pass, with loss scaling and a 32-bit master copy for stability.
why: It roughly halved the memory cost of training, which is part of why billion-parameter models became affordable.
next: Megatron, ZeRO and every large training run since depend on it.
inherits: Reduced precision as the default, now extended to bf16 and fp8.
